questions.prompt: What distinction is central to Chapter 6?
choices: Interest versus novelty
Practice versus talent
Measurement versus praise

explanation.gentle: The chapter separates durable interest from the first rush of novelty.
explanation.direct: Chapter 6 focuses on the difference between returning attraction and opening excitement.
explanation.competitive: It is fighting the lie that buzz equals bond.

questions.prompt: How does the chapter describe durable interest?
choices: As nonstop excitement about the work
As a returning internal pull toward the work
As a reward system created by other people

explanation.gentle: The chapter says interest keeps drawing a person back over time.
explanation.direct: Durable interest is recurring internal return, not permanent hype.
explanation.competitive: The real signal is the pull that keeps reloading.

questions.prompt: Why is pressure-only motivation too weak for long persistence?
choices: Because it is always immoral
Because it fades once the outside force eases
Because it makes interest impossible in every case

explanation.gentle: The chapter says borrowed motivation often weakens when the pressure lifts.
explanation.direct: External force can start action without sustaining durable return.
explanation.competitive: Weak fuel burns bright and dies fast.

choices: Boredom means the interest was definitely fake
Real interest should make every session feel vivid
One dull stretch is too little evidence because genuine attraction can survive boredom

explanation.direct: Chapter 6 would reject the idea that one flat session settles the whole question.
explanation.competitive: A boring block does not get to write the obituary.

questions.prompt: Ava is choosing between a flashy new task and slower work she keeps returning to after the thrill fades. Which chapter reading is strongest?
choices: The flashier option must matter more because it feels stronger now
The slower work may show more durable interest because it still pulls her back
Neither choice says anything about motivation

explanation.gentle: The chapter treats recurring return as stronger evidence than first intensity.
explanation.direct: Durable attraction is tested after novelty weakens.
explanation.competitive: The wrapper can glitter while the deeper pull is somewhere else.

questions.prompt: What question does the chapter recommend asking about your own motivation?
choices: Does this always feel thrilling right now?
What reward do other people want me to chase?
What still draws me back after the first excitement passes?

explanation.gentle: The chapter prefers a question about repeated return after novelty fades.
explanation.direct: It tells you to test durable attraction, not momentary buzz.
explanation.competitive: Ask what keeps hauling you back when the room goes quiet.

questions.prompt: Coach Kim sees a student's excitement dip after week one of a science project. What fits the chapter best?
choices: Treat the dip as proof the student lacks real interest
Help the student reconnect with the part of the work that still sparks curiosity
Replace the project immediately because interest should stay high

explanation.gentle: The chapter suggests looking for recurring attraction under the dip instead of equating the dip with failure.
explanation.direct: A good response is to rebuild re-entry around surviving curiosity.
explanation.competitive: Use the live wire that is still there instead of burying the whole project.

Because growth makes outside pressure irrelevant in every situation
Because interest removes the need for discipline

explanation.direct: Interest follows growth because persistence still needs internal renewal.
explanation.competitive: If the file can change, the next fight is fuel.

questions.prompt: Why does the chapter lead into practice next?
choices: Because attraction alone does not explain how return becomes disciplined improvement
Because practice replaces interest as soon as boredom appears
Because the chapter decides interest is only a form of novelty

explanation.direct: Practice follows because re-entry still needs shaping into better work.
